title: Triangle-wave carrier for a milk frother
prompt: A milk frother's heater is driven by PWM, and the PWM needs a 1 kHz triangle-wave carrier of 2 V peak to peak. Build that oscillator in ngspice using only DC supplies, so the oscillation comes from the circuit itself, and simulate 20 ms. In a .control block, save the carrier voltage with wrdata to a .txt file so it can be plotted.
groundTruth: The netlist, re-run in ngspice offline and the written carrier read back. A triangle comes from integrating a square wave, so a PULSE into an RC, whose ramps curve, fails, and so does any source that is told the time.

checks.label: DC supplies only
checks.how: No PULSE, SIN or PWL source, and no behavioural source that reads time.

checks.label: 1 kHz
checks.how: It runs, oscillates, and settles within 10% of 1 kHz.

checks.label: Straight, even ramps
checks.how: Each ramp fitted to a line with little bend, and rise and fall about equal.

harder: Require a real op-amp model with finite slew and supply rails, so an ideal behavioural comparator is not allowed.
